title: memory-composition-mapper-soft-margin-allocator-for-weights_kv_activations
creator: Liang Chen
description:
Problem: As multi-tenant inference workloads exhibit variable sequence lengths and KV reuse, static splits of GPU memory between weights, KV cache, and activation workspace lead to avoidable OOMs or overly conservative headroom that wastes capacity. We need a compact, deployable model that composes observed telemetry into a live memory budget — a 'memory composition mapper' — which enforces a soft-margin allocation and preemptive, cost-aware rebalancing across weight residency, KV reservoir, and activations.

Goal: Build and ship a soft-margin allocator that: (1) ingests per-GPU telemetry (seq length distribution, KV hit ratio, current kv-resident footprint, activation growth curves), (2) computes a real-time allocation vector for weights/KV/activations plus a small burst buffer, (3) exposes a headroom signal for autoscaler and admission control, and (4) provides graceful degradation rules (eviction order, transient offload to host memory, quantization fallbacks) to avoid hard OOMs while minimizing tail-latency regressions.

Why different: Existing work focuses on predictive headroom or slabbed ledgers; this ticket formalizes a composition model that (a) treats KV as a probabilistic reservoir with hit-rate elasticity, (b) models activations as a stochastic process based on batch mix and sequence percentiles, and (c) reserves a tunable soft-margin rather than fixed watermarks. That enables dynamic redistribution with measurable economic impact (tokens/sec per GPU and OOM frequency).
acceptance_criteria: Memory composition mapper component implemented and compiled into runtime build on staging cluster
End-to-end simulation demonstrates reduction in OOMs by >= 60% on synthetic mixed workloads while keeping 95th-percentile latency delta <= 5%
Exposure of headroom signal via /runtime/telemetry endpoint and Console dashboard with per-GPU breakdown
Rollback policy and graceful-degradation rules documented and validated in canary runs
Automated test coverage for allocation math and eviction ordering added (unit + integration)
Performance regression < 2% CPU overhead for mapper compute under typical telemetry rate

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect telemetry leads to oscillation in allocations. Mitigation: add dampening window and minimum hysteresis, require 3 stable windows before rebalancing.
Risk: Eviction increases tail latency for active sessions. Mitigation: prefer LRU by request-affinity, implement short grace TTL and fallback to quantized weight variant before eviction.
Risk: Mapper CPU cost affects runtime. Mitigation: offload heavy math to async worker and limit compute to per-second cadence with delta thresholds.
Risk: Cross-tenant fairness issues when rebalancing on shared GPUs. Mitigation: per-tenant soft-quotas and proportional shrink with priority tags.
Risk: Unexpected OOMs during rollout. Mitigation: strict canary thresholds and automated rollback on OOM spike > 2x baseline.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: deterministic slab allocation vs probabilistic reservoir modeling; we chose probabilistic reservoir to better utilize KV when hit rates are high and reclaim when hit rates drop.
Soft-margin parameterization: default margin = 6% of GPU memory on p4d, adjustable per-cluster via config map.
Eviction order: candidate priority = (kv_access_freq * weight) / resident_size; low frequency large shards evicted first.
Prefetch policy: prefetch recent KV prefixes for long-running chats; avoid prefetch for short single-turn requests to reduce KV pressure.
